question: Tell me about a time you improved a process or workflow.
answer: In a previous role, I noticed that our team spent a significant amount of time manually compiling information from multiple sources into weekly reports. The process was repetitive, time-consuming, and occasionally led to errors because information had to be copied and checked several times before the report could be finalized. I began by observing how different team members completed the task and documenting each step involved. After identifying the most time-consuming areas, I proposed creating a standardized workflow that included templates, automated data collection where possible, and clearer responsibilities for different stages of the reporting process. To implement the change, I collaborated with colleagues to test the new workflow on a smaller scale before rolling it out to the entire team. During the pilot phase, we gathered feedback and made adjustments based on practical challenges that emerged. The final process reduced manual effort, improved consistency across reports, and allowed team members to spend more time analyzing information rather than gathering it. Beyond the efficiency gains, the project also highlighted the value of continuous improvement and showed how small operational changes can create meaningful benefits over time.
